sanskrit: na tvā pratyabhijānāmi kim idaṃ bharatarṣabha śrotavyaṃ cen mayā pārtha kṣipram ākhyātum arhasi
english: I do not recognize you as the man you were. What has happened, O bull of the Bharatas? If it is fit for me to hear, O Pārtha, you should tell it to me at once.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yaḥ sa medhavapuḥ śrīmān bṛhatpaṅkajalocanaḥ sa kṛṣṇaḥ saha rāmeṇa tyaktvā dehaṃ divaṃ gataḥ
english: Arjuna said: He whose body was the very form of wisdom, the glorious one with great lotus eyes—that Kṛṣṇa, together with Rāma, has cast off his body and gone to heaven.

sanskrit: mausale vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ vināśo brahmaśāpajaḥ babhūva vīrāntakaraḥ prabhāse romaharṣaṇaḥ
english: At the battle of the iron clubs, born of a brahmin's curse, the destruction of the Vṛṣṇi heroes came to pass at Prabhāsa—a slaughter of warriors that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: ye te śūrā mahātmānaḥ siṃhadarpā mahābalāḥ bhojavṛṣṇyandhakā brahmann anyonyaṃ tair hataṃ yudhi
english: Those valiant, great-souled men, proud as lions and mighty in strength, the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, O brahmin—by one another they were slain in battle.

sanskrit: gadāparighaśaktīnāṃ sahāḥ parighabāhavaḥ ta erakābhir nihatāḥ paśya kālasya paryayam
english: Men who could withstand maces, iron bars, and spears, whose arms were like iron clubs—they were struck down by mere blades of eraka grass. Behold the turning of Time!

sanskrit: hataṃ pañcaśataṃ teṣāṃ sahasraṃ bāhuśālinām nidhanaṃ samanuprāptaṃ samāsādyetaretaram
english: Five hundred thousand of those strong-armed warriors were slain; they met their end by falling upon one another.

sanskrit: punaḥ punar na mṛśyāmi vināśam amitaujasām cintayāno yadūnāṃ ca kṛṣṇasya ca yaśasvinaḥ
english: Again and again I cannot bear it, brooding upon the destruction of those of immeasurable might—of the Yadus and of the glorious Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: śoṣaṇaṃ sāgarasyeva parvatasyeva cālanam nabhasaḥ patanaṃ caiva śaityam agnes tathaiva ca
english: It is like the drying up of the ocean, the shaking of a mountain, the falling of the sky, and the cold of fire.

sanskrit: aśraddheyam ahaṃ manye vināśaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ na ceha sthātum icchāmi loke kṛṣṇavinākṛtaḥ
english: Unbelievable I hold the destruction of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; and I have no wish to remain here in this world, parted from Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: itaḥ kaṣṭataraṃ cānyac chṛṇu tad vai tapodhana mano me dīryate yena cintayānasya vai muhuḥ
english: And hear of another thing more grievous still than this, O you whose wealth is austerity—a thing by which, as I brood on it again and again, my heart is torn asunder.

sanskrit: paśyato vṛṣṇidārāś ca mama brahman sahasraśaḥ ābhīrair anusṛtyājau hṛtāḥ pañcanadālayaiḥ
english: Before my very eyes, O brahmin, the women of the Vṛṣṇis, by the thousands, were carried off in a fight—pursued and seized by the Ābhīras who dwell in the land of the Five Rivers.

sanskrit: dhanur ādāya tatrāhaṃ nāśakaṃ tasya pūraṇe yathā purā ca me vīryaṃ bhujayor na tathābhavat
english: Taking up my bow there, I could not even bend it to string it, and the strength of my arms was not as it once had been.

sanskrit: astrāṇi me pranaṣṭāni vividhāni mahāmune śarāś ca kṣayam āpannāḥ kṣaṇenaiva samantataḥ
english: My weapons of many kinds had vanished from me, O great sage, and my arrows ran out on every side in but an instant.

sanskrit: puruṣaś cāprameyātmā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ caturbhujaḥ pītavāsā śyāmaḥ padmāyatekṣaṇaḥ
english: And that Person of immeasurable soul, bearing conch, discus, and mace, four-armed, clad in yellow, dark of hue, with eyes long as lotus petals—

sanskrit: yaḥ sa yāti purastān me rathasya sumahādyutiḥ pradahan ripusainyāni na paśyāmy aham adya tam
english: he who used to go before my chariot, of exceedingly great splendor, burning up the armies of the foe—him I see no longer today.

sanskrit: yena pūrvaṃ pradagdhāni śatrusainyāni tejasā śarair gāṇḍīvanirmuktair ahaṃ paścād vyanāśayam
english: He by whose splendor the enemy hosts were first scorched—those I then destroyed afterward with the arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: tam apaśyan viṣīdāmi ghūrṇāmīva ca sattama parinirviṇṇacetāś ca śāntiṃ nopalabhe 'pi ca
english: Not seeing him, I sink in despair and reel as if dizzy, O best of men; and with a heart utterly weary, I cannot find any peace at all.

sanskrit: vinā janārdanaṃ vīraṃ nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe śrutvaiva hi gataṃ viṣṇuṃ mamāpi mumuhur diśaḥ
english: Without the hero Janārdana I have no will to live; for at the mere hearing that Viṣṇu was gone, the very quarters of the sky grew bewildered before me.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭajñātivīryasya śūnyasya paridhāvataḥ upadeṣṭuṃ mama śreyo bhavān arhati sattama
english: To me, whose kinsmen and whose strength are utterly lost, empty and wandering aimlessly, you should counsel what is best, O best of men.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca brahmaśāpavinirdagdhā vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathāḥ vinaṣṭāḥ kuruśārdūla na tāñ śocitum arhasi
english: Vyāsa said: Burned up by a brahmin's curse, the great warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas have perished, O tiger of the Kurus; you ought not to grieve for them.

sanskrit: bhavitavyaṃ tathā tad dhi diṣṭam etan mahātmanām upekṣitaṃ ca kṛṣṇena śaktenāpi vyapohitum
english: For it was bound to be so; this was the fate ordained for those great souls, and Kṛṣṇa, though able to turn it aside, let it be.

sanskrit: trailokyam api kṛṣṇo hi kṛtsnaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam prasahed anyathā kartuṃ kim u śāpaṃ manīṣiṇām
english: For Kṛṣṇa could have made the whole threefold world, with all that moves and stands still, to be otherwise—how much more the curse of the wise!

sanskrit: rathasya purato yāti yaḥ sa cakragadādharaḥ tava snehāt purāṇarṣir vāsudevaś caturbhujaḥ
english: He who went before your chariot, bearer of discus and mace—that ancient seer, the four-armed Vāsudeva—did so out of love for you.

sanskrit: kṛtvā bhārāvataraṇaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pṛthulocanaḥ mokṣayitvā jagat sarvaṃ gataḥ svasthānam uttamam
english: Having lifted the burden from the earth, the large-eyed one, having delivered the whole world, has gone to his own supreme abode.

sanskrit: tvayā tv iha mahat karma devānāṃ puruṣarṣabha kṛtaṃ bhīmasahāyena yamābhyāṃ ca mahābhuja
english: By you, O bull among men, a great work for the gods has here been accomplished, with Bhīma as your helper and with the twins, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyāṃś ca vo manye saṃsiddhān kurupuṃgava gamanaṃ prāptakālaṃ ca tad dhi śreyo mataṃ mama
english: I deem you to have fulfilled your purpose and attained your end, O foremost of the Kurus; the time for your departure has come, and that I hold to be the best course for you.

sanskrit: balaṃ buddhiś ca tejaś ca pratipattiś ca bhārata bhavanti bhavakāleṣu vipadyante viparyaye
english: Strength, intellect, splendor, and resolve, O Bhārata, arise in the times of their flourishing and fail when the time turns adverse.

sanskrit: kālamūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagadbījaṃ dhanaṃjaya kāla eva samādatte punar eva yadṛcchayā
english: All this has Time for its root; Time is the seed of the world, O Dhanaṃjaya. Time alone gathers it back again at its own will.

sanskrit: sa eva balavān bhūtvā punar bhavati durbalaḥ sa eveśaś ca bhūtveha parair ājñāpyate punaḥ
english: That same man, having grown strong, becomes weak again; and he, having become a lord here, is once more commanded by others.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyāni cāstrāṇi gatāny adya yathāgatam punar eṣyanti te hastaṃ yadā kālo bhaviṣyati
english: Your weapons, their work accomplished, have today gone the way by which they came; they will return again to your hand when the time shall be.

sanskrit: kālo gantuṃ gatiṃ mukhyāṃ bhavatām api bhārata etac chreyo hi vo manye paramaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: It is time for you too to go upon the highest path, O Bhārata; this I hold to be your supreme good, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: etad vacanam ājñāya vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ anujñāto yayau pārtho nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Heeding this counsel of Vyāsa of boundless splendor, and granted leave, Pārtha set out for the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: praviśya ca purīṃ vīraḥ samāsādya yudhiṣṭhiram ācaṣṭa tad yathāvṛttaṃ vṛṣṇyandhakajanaṃ prati
english: And the hero, entering the city and coming to Yudhiṣṭhira, related all that had happened concerning the people of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, just as it had occurred.
